items.excerpt: In this Crunchbase News Q&A, longtime global investor Jeremy Kranz shares his vision for his firm Sentinel Global, and observations about, among other things, the race to AI dominance and what the U.S. can do to bridge the gap.

items.excerpt: As AI reshapes industries, True Ventures sees echoes of the Web 2.0 era that launched it decades ago. With more than 80 AI investments, True is focusing on the application layer, where it expects the next decade’s most valuable companies to emerge.

items.excerpt: San Francisco-based Denki, which has built AI-powered software for financial auditors at public companies, has raised $4.1 million in funding, the startup tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

items.excerpt: A total of 37 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in March, the highest monthly count in close to four years, Crunchbase data shows. The robotics sector led unicorn creation last month, with six new billion-dollar startups.
items.title: The New Unicorn Count Reached A 4-Year High In March, Led By Robotics, Frontier Labs And AI Infrastructure

items.excerpt: Technical expertise still matters, but when everyone can build, thanks to AI, it no longer differentiates, writes guest author Aaron Tainter, director of accelerator programs at Innovation Works. And that forces a harder question for investors: If the product isn’t the moat, what is?
items.title: AI Is Rewriting What Investors Should Look For In Early Startup Teams

items.excerpt: Digital banking startup Mercury has raised $200 million in a Series D round at a $5.2 billion valuation, the company announced Wednesday. That’s up 49% from the $3.5 billion valuation it achieved when announcing its $300 million Series C — which included primary and secondary funding — in March of 2
items.title: Digital Banking Startup Mercury Lands $200M At $5.2B Valuation Amid Fintech Funding Uptick

items.excerpt: Reports of “SaaS being dead” are misguided, writes guest author Bob Morse, who contends that AI will enable software companies to move beyond selling productivity tools to deliver knowledge-work outcomes directly, unlocking massive unmet demand for services, ultimately growing the software industry.
items.title: SaaS Is Dead. Long Live SaaS! AI And The End Of The Rationing Of Knowledge Work

items.excerpt: This week was not an exceptionally busy one for large funding deals, though we saw sizable rounds in a lively mix of sectors ranging from AI to fintech to quantum computing, biotech and cybersecurity.

items.excerpt: When building your brand you need to play to the demands of customers, investors and potential employees. Jenny Sagström of creative agency Sköna, provides tips on getting and keeping the attention of these three key audiences.
items.title: B2B Brand Building For Series B And Beyond

items.excerpt: Perplexity AI is reportedly nearing completion of a funding round that will give the AI search startup a unicorn valuation of around $1 billion.
items.title: Perplexity Poised To Become Latest AI Startup To Hit Unicorn Status — Report

items.excerpt: Startups working on ways to combat disinformation and misinformation have continued to see venture investment flow their way.
items.title: More Funding Goes To Startups Fighting Disinformation

items.excerpt: Nearly half of food service employers today say they need more workers. Theoretically, automation could go a long way to ease the labor shortage.
items.title: Restaurant Robotics Revs Up Amid Labor Shortages

items.excerpt: As furry friends age, their people face the prospect of costly vet bills, chronic health conditions to manage, and constant worry about their companions’ well-being, so it’s not surprising to see funding to startups conceived around the needs of older animals.
items.title: Old Dogs Can Inspire New Business Models

items.excerpt: Typically, when a venture-backed startup raises a follow-on round, the size of the investment and the company’s valuation go up as well. Lately, however, sequential rounds aren’t always getting bigger. We look at the Crunchbase data.
items.title: The Shrinking Series E: More Senior Startups Raise Smaller Follow-On Rounds

items.excerpt: The same day Perplexity AI announced a $62.7 million round, it was reported the AI startup is looking to raise another $250 million-plus at a valuation between $2.5 billion and $3 billion.
items.title: Perplexity Looks To Raise $250M-Plus At Valuation Of $2.5B Or More — Report

items.excerpt: Retail has a growing category of investors still not considered by many founders as a potential source of funding, writes guest author Mila Khrapchenko, who shares ways a startup can catch their attention and possibly investment dollars.
items.title: 4 Things To Consider If You Want To Raise Startup Funds From Retail Investors

items.excerpt: How long will investors wait for a public company to produce net income? We focused on companies that went public after 2000 and are currently among the very large cap stocks. Here’s what we found.
items.title: To Make It Big, Most Tech Startups Have A Limited Post-IPO Window To Turn Profitable

items.excerpt: The very qualities and skills that enable a founder to establish a company and drive its early success can sometimes hinder business growth, argues Mikhail Taver of Taver Capital. In this commentary he explains why the answer may be to bring in new leadership and how to do that smoothly.
items.title: Why Successful Founders Sometimes Need To Step Aside — And How To Do It

items.excerpt: Financial aspects of an M&A deal are only part of the equation, writes Jason Williams, chief talent officer for Thomson Reuters, who shares what he’s learned about the importance of culture and talent in determining how successfully two companies will work together.
items.title: Cultural Collateral: Why People Are Important For A Successful M&A Transaction

items.excerpt: While growth hacking and marketing automation strategies are critical, in fintech, the warm introduction remains undefeated, writes guest author Itay Sagie. In this article he shares why personal connections can be the ultimate funding alliance.
items.title: Why Connections And Compliance Beat Code In Fintech Sales

items.excerpt: We recently spoke with Tiffany Luck, a partner at New Enterprise Associates about the increasing relevance of vertical AI, how startups can carve out durable advantages in a world dominated by platform giants, and more.
items.title: NEA’s Tiffany Luck On How Startup Founders Can Build Moats In Vertical AI

items.title: How I Raised $14M For My Startup When I Stopped Pitching And Started Speaking

items.excerpt: While cloud migration previously offered unmatched speed and cost efficiency, decision-makers now perceive localized systems as offering superior long-term security. items.title: Is On-Prem Making A Comeback?
